rationale: The Latin anchors *compensatio*, *emendatio*, and *reparatio* all point to making amends or compensating for a wrong, while the legal attestations (L. Ethb., L. Alf. pol.) situate BÓT firmly in the Old English legal sense of reparation/compensation for an offense. This aligns squarely with atonement.n.01 ("compensation for a wrong"), as illustrated by its own example "we were unable to get satisfaction from the local store," rather than the more abstract contentment senses or the purely financial/debt sense of satisfaction.n.04.
